newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB says current trading "well ahead" of 96.
newsitem.headline: AIB says current trading "well ahead" of 96.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks Plc said on Wednesday that trading in the first four months of 1997 had been strong and across all divisions performance was "well ahead" of 1996 levels.

"In the first four months of 1997 trading has been -- and continues to be -- strong. Across all AIB's divisions, this performance is well ahead of results recorded this time last year," chairman Lochlann Quinn told the company's annual meeting.
Quinn said the bank's success was built on using its brand to good effect, its enhanced customer service and its "number one position in banking technology applications in Ireland."
He said the AIB was well placed to cope with the onset of economic and monetary union (EMU).
"We are entering (a) time of great change," Quinn said. "I am confident of our ability to adapt and prosper in that new environment."
AIB announced in January it was buying Pennsylvania bank Dauphin Deposit Corp for $1.36 billion. The acquisition has been cleared by the Federal Reserve and Dauphin's shareholders.
Quinn described the acquisition as "without doubt the most significant development in the group's recent history and the largest undertaken by an Irish company."
He said AIB's increased investment in Poland's WBK Bank was another highlight of 1996.
Overall, AIB's 1996 performance had been "impressive in all divisions," Quinn said.
